units.note: Distances (100 ft, 50 ft, 200 ft) and the οὔτε…οὔτε…πλὴν τελείως ὀλίγων clause check.

findings.quote: place the market-place, quartermaster’s office, and headquarters between the two camps
findings.problem: μέσον τιθέασι τῶν δυεῖν στρατοπέδων: here στρατόπεδον means legion, as everywhere in this section (εἰς ἕκαστον στρατόπεδον = 'each legion', translated so in this same chapter). A consul camping on his own with his two legions puts the forum, quaestorium and praetorium between those two legions, not 'between the two camps', which would wrongly suggest the two consuls' separate camps.
findings.proposed_fix: place the market-place, quartermaster’s office, and headquarters between the two legions

units.note: This is a referent-identity error (legion vs camp), the closest of the listed classes being wrong identity. Numbers (4,000/5,000; double area; perimeter half as much again) check.

findings.quote: the duty falls to each maniple only once every four days
findings.problem: παρὰ τετάρτην ἡμέραν counts inclusively: 'every third day'. That agrees with the arithmetic, since three maniples take turns (ἀνὰ μέρος) serving each tribune, so each serves one day in three. 'Once every four days' is wrong by one.
findings.proposed_fix: the duty falls to each maniple only every third day

units.note: τῷ γειτνιῶντι κατόπιν τῶν οὐλαμῶν is spatially loose (guard posted behind the squadrons vs squadron behind the maniple). Paton reads it the same way as the current English, so no finding.

The Greek breaks off mid-sentence (τοῦ κατὰ φυλακὴν) and continues at the head of ch. 36 with βουκανᾶν. That is a chapter seam, not a lacuna, so the English 'sounding the bugle' is correctly supplied from 36.1.
